coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app contains zero tests of its own; none of the risky data-transformation, pagination, URL-state or error paths are covered by anything the team owns.

regression_power.rationale: With no app-owned tests, any regression in the pure logic or the client interactivity would be caught only if the external acceptance suite happens to sample that exact case.

evidence: app/src/ — no test files, so no noise; the shared/ pure-function layer (format.js, home-view.js, router.js) shows the code was factored to be easily testable but never tested
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value tests; scored 3 per the rubric, but the absence is a missed opportunity rather than a virtue.

findings.issue: No test runner, no test script, and zero test files anywhere in app/ (~700 significant LOC of non-trivial logic)
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (already a vite project) and unit-test the shared/ pure modules first: filterSummaries, homeResultsHtml, parseHomeState, homeQueryString, humanize, latestEnglishFlavor, matchRoute

findings.issue: Filtering, 48-per-page slicing, total-pages math, page clamping and default-omitting URL construction are untested; off-by-one or clamp bugs and ?page=999 inconsistencies would slip through
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests over filterSummaries/homeResultsHtml/parseHomeState covering page 0, page > total, non-numeric page, empty results, and q with URL-reserved characters

findings.issue: Client-side sort comparator untested: numeric-vs-text dispatch, missing-values-sort-last in descending order, direction flip and aria-sort housekeeping can all regress under refactor
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator into shared/ and unit-test it (missing values, numeric strings, em-dash cells, ascending/descending), plus a DOM-level test that aria-sort moves between headers

findings.issue: Hidden-ability marker is keyed by Pokémon id (idFromUrl(entry.pokemon.url)) but looked up by species.id; they diverge on the fallback mapping path, silently dropping the 'Hidden ability' text
findings.suggestion: Key the map by the resolved species id, and add a test with a Pokémon whose species id differs from its Pokémon id

findings.issue: Debounce (200 ms) races with the popstate handler: type then immediately press Back and the stale debounce re-renders content that no longer matches the URL
findings.suggestion: Clear the pending debounce in the popstate handler; add an integration test for type-then-back

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent(match[2]) throws URIError on malformed percent-encoding (/pokemon/%), turning a should-be-404 into a 500
findings.suggestion: Wrap in try/catch (or validate the segment) and return the not-found route; unit-test matchRoute with malformed input

findings.issue: Promise-cache eviction/retry pattern (cache.delete on rejection, summariesPromise reset) is unguarded; a getJson refactor that caches rejected promises or drops the reset would leave the app permanently broken after one API hiccup
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getJson against a stubbed fetch: 404 → NotFoundError, 500 → error, then success on retry (cache must not hold the rejection)

findings.issue: All API failures collapse to a bare text/plain 500; no user-facing error page and no test exercises API-down behaviour
findings.suggestion: Render an in-app error page for render failures and add an integration test with an unreachable API_BASE_URL

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavor / collapseWhitespace (\f and \n runs, mixed-language entries), formatMeters rounding and dexNumber padding are untested despite being spec-defined
findings.suggestion: Cheap property/table tests over the format helpers; they are pure and already exported

findings.issue: buildSummaries fetches ~1,025 pokemon records on first home request (concurrency 32) with no persistence; per-process warm-up cost and partial-failure behaviour are untested
findings.suggestion: Add a warm-up on server start plus a test that a mid-build fetch failure is retried rather than cached

summary: The app ships with no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no spec files — so all regression protection comes from the harness-owned acceptance suite. Ironically, the architecture is well set up for testing: filtering, pagination, URL state and formatting live in pure shared modules that would be trivial to unit-test. Until those are covered, a refactor of the data layer or the client sort comparator could break pagination edge cases, the hidden-ability marker, sorting of missing values, and not-found handling with no failing test in the repo.
